summary: The artifact ships a broad, well-organised Phase 3 state layer — a canonical serializable ProgramState (32 slots + 8 Live), Store/dirty/discard, splits/zones/crossfades, scenes, morph assignments, master clock, transpose and Panic — and a single-AudioContext graph in which every engine is mixed inside one System4 DSP core and drains through one master gain + limiter to one destination. All four technical checks pass (151/151 tests in 16 files, typecheck, lint, build). Program browsing, Store, dirty 'E', edit-discard and Live auto-store were verified end-to-end through the built app at artifact/dist. Beyond that layer the delivered instrument diverges sharply from its own claims. In an unmodified browser the app makes no sound at all: the AudioContext is constructed eagerly at mount and resume() appears nowhere in src or in the shipped bundle, so it stays 'suspended' after user gesture and the ScriptProcessor drain never fires (0 audioprocess callbacks measured). Forcing the context to run exposes the engines: the Synth's state-variable filter is unconditionally unstable (its state matrix has an eigenvalue 1 + u(1+sqrt5)/2 > 1 for every cutoff), so a clean A440 sine renders as a saturated rail — dc 0.698, ac-rms 0.033, 1 zero crossing in 0.2 s — all five source categories rail identically, and LP24/HP emit non-finite samples. Two of the nine factory programs ('4.4 FM Bell', '5.5 Band Layered') render 100% non-finite samples at the master output, destroying the piano and organ layers in those programs too. The Organ is genuinely functional — pitched, drawbar-shaped, with working percussion, key click, vibrato/chorus and Rotary — but every non-Farf model rides a DC offset several times its audio content, and Vox is B3 minus two partials (mean-removed correlation 0.9993) where the spec requires a distinct engine; B3 Bass and Pipe 2 reuse is explicitly permitted. The arpeggiator computes a step index that never reaches the audio path (run on/off is bit-identical). The keybed — 46% of the instrument — renders as one blank white slab because unit key coordinates are emitted as CSS percentages (left 100%/200%, width 100%): 1 of 73 keys lands inside the viewport, no black keys are visible, and pointer/touch note input is dead because the absolutely-positioned black-key container covers the whole keybed. That same slab is visible in the artifact's own sealed captures. The panel is also decoupled from the instrument: nothing writes program state back into the hardware store, so after any program change all 236 controls still show the previous patch (a split program shows Split off; an organ program leaves the drawbars where they were), and a control whose stale value already matches the program silently does nothing. Panel coverage is thinner than the engine besides: the morph wheel is never connected (setWheel/setPedal have no caller in src), there is no control-pedal control, split editing is a single hard-coded C4 toggle whose low zone is unplayable anyway (the only working input spans MIDI 60..83 and the split point is 60), drawbar bindings are mis-scaled (one keyboard step takes a drawbar from 8 to 1), and ~20 non-excluded controls (effects focus/group/global, Rotary on/speed, To Rotary A/B, synth filter type, piano section on/focus/model, mod wheel, pitch stick) are inert in Phase 3 because they are only handled by the superseded Phase 2 bridge. Tests are numerous but prove little where it matters: engine distinctness is asserted as |RMS difference| > 1e-5, which passes on DC rails and on gain-scaled copies; the '11 documented split positions' test asserts two literal arrays declared inside the test file; and no test renders a factory program end-to-end, which is why 100%-NaN output ships green.

criteria.label: Reference and regression retention
evidence: Deck retention is real: the built app at artifact/dist serves 6 sections (.section count = 6) in the documented order at fractions 0.14/0.20/0.085/0.125/0.25/0.20 (artifact/src/hardware/sections.ts:196-240), a continuous red chassis, dark inset panels, two OLEDs (Program, Synth) and 236 aria-labelled controls; this matches evidence/stage1-desktop.png and evidence/stage2-desktop.png.

Keybed is a blank white slab, not 73 keys: artifact/src/hardware/keys.ts:38-39,63-69 emits unit coordinates (white key x = 0..42, width = 1) which artifact/src/components/Keybed.tsx:68 renders as `left: ${x*100}%; width: ${width*100}%`. Measured in headless Chromium against dist: key 'E1 (MIDI 28)' rect = 1301px wide at left 70px (style left 0%, width 100%), 'F1 (MIDI 29)' at left 1370px (style left 100%), 'G1' at left 2671px (style left 200%); 1 of 73 key elements and 0 of 30 black keys fall inside the 1440x900 viewport.

The defect is in the sealed evidence, not the evaluation environment: artifact/evidence/stage3-desktop.png shows the same featureless white rectangle with a single 'E1' label where the keybed should be, and an independent capture of dist reproduces it.

Against inputs/reference/nord-stage-4-73.jpg (43 white + 30 black keys with visible seams occupying the lower ~45% of the instrument) the final capture loses the entire keybed pattern — the single most prominent feature of the variant.

Narrow retention is intact: at 390x844 document.scrollWidth == clientWidth == 390 (no horizontal overflow), all six sections and all 73 key elements still render (evidence/stage3-narrow.png), so the responsive frame itself has not drifted.
Review note: the deck itself is strong enough that a rating of 2 is also defensible; 1 is kept because the criterion names geometry explicitly and the lost element is 46% of the instrument.

criteria.label: Complete hardware state fidelity
evidence: The panel never reflects the loaded program. Stepping through six factory programs in dist and reading control state each time: P1.1 'Grand Piano', P1.4 '3.2 B3 Organ' (program drawbars [6,4,8,6,4,2,1,0,0]), P1.6 '4.1 Synth Pad', P1.8 '5.1 Split' (split.on = true), P2.1 '5.5 Band Layered' and P3.5 all left 'Piano layer B on' aria-checked=false, '8 foot drawbar' aria-valuenow=8, '16 foot drawbar'=0, 'S1 level'=0.7 and 'Split' aria-checked=false. artifact/src/App.tsx:160-165 (reflectDisplays) pushes only the two OLED strings; no program -> hardware-store path exists.

The desync also silences controls: src/system/bridge.ts:218-233 applies deltas only, so a control whose stale panel value already equals the program's value no-ops. Reproduced on P1.2 '2.1 Upright Combo' (which has piano layer B enabled while the panel reads false): clicking 'Piano layer B on' changed nothing and raised no dirty 'E'.

Working hardware state: the Program OLED tracks the loaded program ('1.1 Grand Piano' -> '3.2 B3 Organ' -> '4.1 Synth Pad'), the readout shows P{page}.{button} and appends 'E' when dirty (observed 'P1.1E' after an edit, cleared by two Store presses), latching buttons expose role=switch + aria-checked, momentary buttons expose aria-pressed, and knobs/faders/drawbars expose role=slider with aria-valuenow/valuetext (artifact/src/components/controls/controls.tsx).

Drawbar state display is corrupted by a scale mismatch: the store holds 0..8 (artifact/src/hardware/sections.ts:22-30) but DrawbarControl feeds useDragValue a normalised 0..1 value and writes that back (controls.tsx:127-133). Measured in dist: '8 foot drawbar' aria-valuenow 8 -> ArrowDown -> 1 -> ArrowDown -> 0, and artifact/src/system/bridge.ts:79 then rounds that 0..1 number into drawbars[2].

Transpose readout does not refresh on change: App.tsx:100-101 calls engine.setTranspose, and System4.setTranspose (artifact/src/audio/system4.ts:395-397) mutates working state without emit(); after two 'Transpose up' presses the strip still read 0, jumping to '+2' only when an unrelated edit forced a re-render.

State without behaviour: the drawbar LED graph controls expose no value (aria-valuenow null on '8 foot drawbar level graph'), the Modulation wheel moves (aria-valuenow 0 -> 1) but is not connected to anything, and the effects focus/global/To-Rotary/Rotary buttons light up while driving nothing in Phase 3 (see hardwareBindings).

criteria.label: Programs and Live Mode
evidence: Exercised end-to-end in the built app (Playwright against artifact/dist): program buttons 1-8 select within the page, Page up/down move by 8 (P1.4 -> P2.4), the dial nudges (artifact/src/system/bridge.ts:192-201), and the Program OLED follows the stored name.
Dirty/Store verified directly on the readout: clean 'P1.1' -> edit -> 'P1.1E' -> Store -> 'P1.1E' (armed) -> Store -> 'P1.1' (System4.storePress/storeConfirm, system4.ts:207-236).

Live Mode: clicking Live Mode shows 'LIVE', an edit made there auto-stored (System4.markEdited, system4.ts:168-174) and survived leaving and re-entering Live Mode — the 8 Live slots behave as auto-storing.

32 regular + 8 Live slots and >=8 factory programs are real (system4.ts:31-32,127-131; artifact/src/system/factory.ts:139-190), verified by tests/system.test.ts:40-141. Edit-discard on program change is proven by tests/system.test.ts and the dirty flag, not by panel readings — panel controls never re-read program state, so their values are not evidence either way (see completeHardwareState).

Gaps: Store As with naming exists only on the engine (system4.ts:245-251) with no panel affordance anywhere in src, and the numeric list view required by programs.navigation is absent from the UI — the test named for it (tests/system.test.ts:157-182) only exercises index arithmetic.

criteria.label: Layers, splits, scenes, and morphs
evidence: Engine-level behaviour is real: with split on at C4 and zone piano.A = {low:0,high:1}, note 55 fires (rms 0.0211) and note 64 fires nothing; setting crossfade.mid = 12 makes note 64 fire at rms 0.0109 and crossfade 6 at 0.0076, i.e. the Off/+-6/+-12 crossfade gains really attenuate (artifact/src/audio/system4.ts:51-84).

Scenes work: with scenes.II disabling piano.A, switching to Scene II changes the rendered mix (rms 0.1260 -> 0.1243, peak 0.2353 -> 0.1927) and only the enable mask differs (system4.ts:253-262, 584-589).

Clock/transpose/Panic work: tap tempo and setTempo clamp to 30..300 (system4.ts:371-393), transpose shifts routed notes (system4.ts:512-527), and Panic dropped voiceCount to 0 with post-Panic master-output rms 0.000000 in a browser capture.

Morphs are unreachable from the instrument: System4.setWheel/setPedal (system4.ts:315-323) have no caller anywhere in src (grep 'setWheel|setPedal' -> system4.ts definitions plus tests/splits.test.ts only). Moving the Modulation wheel in dist changed aria-valuenow with no effect on the mix, and there is no Control Pedal input in the surface inventory at all (artifact/src/hardware/sections.ts:12-18) — only the prog.morph-pedal assign button.

Split editing from the panel is a single hard-coded toggle: bridge.ts:207 -> System4.toggleSplit (system4.ts:264-270) forces split.points.mid = 60. No control exists for the 11 documented split positions, for crossfade width, or for per-layer zone assignment, so the hard gate 'splits, crossfades, scenes, morphs and layer routing are editable from the panel' is met only for scenes.

The split low zone is not merely uneditable but unplayable: the only working note input is the computer keyboard, which spans MIDI 60..83 (src/piano/inputs.ts:12-14), and the split point is 60, so no note below the split can be sounded (pointer input is dead, MIDI unavailable).
Layer focus is decorative: piano.layer-a/b-focus, synth.s1/s2/s3-focus and fx.focus-* are declared controls with no binding in the Phase 3 bridge.

criteria.label: Complete Organ system
evidence: The organ makes a real, pitched sound and drawbars shape it: a single 8' drawbar at A440 measured 183 zero crossings in 0.2 s at 48 kHz (expected ~176); changing the registration moves the spectral centroid (148 Hz -> 767 Hz). Percussion, key click (peak 0.353 -> 0.313 with click off) and vibrato/chorus each measurably change the render, and Rotary is a genuine shared instance with slow/fast/stop + drive (organ.ts:121-126,239).

Of the four required-distinct models (inputs/specs/nord-stage-4.organ.json: B3, Vox, Farf, Pipe 1), one is a duplicate. Rendering MIDI 60 at 48 kHz with drawbars [8,6,8,6,5,4,3,2,2] and correlating with the DC component removed: B3 vs Vox 0.9993 (Vox is the B3 partial list minus two partials, organ.ts:47-56, and the spec's filtered/unfiltered mix drawbar is admittedly not implemented), B3 vs Pipe1 0.827, Farf 0.69-0.85 against everything else. B3 Bass ('may-reuse-B3') and Pipe 2 ('may-reuse-Pipe-1') are explicitly permitted reuses and are not counted against this criterion.

Every non-Farf model carries a large DC offset: the voice sums partials as 0.55 + 0.45*sin (organ.ts:289), so a single 8' drawbar renders dc 0.1227 against ac-rms 0.0668, and the '3.2 B3 Organ' factory program measured in-browser at dc 0.186 against ac-rms 0.055 — the tone is a small ripple riding a DC step, which costs headroom and thumps on note events.

Panel control of the organ is partial and partly broken: the drawbar binding is mis-scaled (one keyboard step from 8 lands on 1, see completeHardwareState), the drawbar LED graphs expose aria-valuenow null, the four model buttons force BOTH layers to the same model (bridge.ts:86-89), 'organ.level' only drives layer A (bridge.ts:95), and no control enables/disables the organ section, its second layer, or the octave — the two-layer organ is reachable only by loading a program, and loading a program does not move the drawbars.
The effects-section Rotary on / To Rotary A/B buttons are inert in Phase 3, so rotary routing is program-only; morphable rotary speed is unreachable because morphs are unreachable.

criteria.label: Complete Synth system
evidence: The synth engine does not produce a waveform. A single Pure/Sine voice at A440 with the effect chain bypassed, res 0, keytrack 0, no filter envelope renders dc 0.6984 / ac-rms 0.0326 / ac-peak 0.6984 with 1 zero crossing in 0.2 s at 48 kHz, and identically at cutoff 0.1/0.3/0.5/0.9; the first samples show an exponential runaway from 0 to the 0.7 rail in ~30 samples. The cause is structural: the state-variable filter in artifact/src/audio/synth.ts:349-357 has state matrix [[1+u,-u],[-u,1]] with u = g/(1+g(g+k)), whose larger eigenvalue 1 + u(1+sqrt5)/2 exceeds 1 for every positive cutoff, so it is unconditionally unstable and clamps at renderLayer (synth.ts:283).

Consequently the five required categories are indistinguishable: rendering Pure/Sync/Multi/Super/FM-H at 48 kHz gives raw pairwise correlation 0.9995-1.0000 for all ten pairs (0.84-0.99 even with DC removed), with dc 0.698 and 1 zero crossing each.

Filter types HP and LP24 emit non-finite samples: filterType 2 and 1 produced 7457 of 9600 samples each. In the browser this reaches the master output — the '4.4 FM Bell' program rendered 19132/20480 non-finite samples on one key and 20480/20480 on another.

The arpeggiator/gate is state-only: advanceArp (synth.ts:384-398) updates c.arpStep/c.arpNote, but arpNote is never read by renderLayer or osc(). Rendering three held notes with arp.run false vs true gives a sum-absolute-difference of exactly 0. tests/synth.test.ts:177-240 asserts only eng.arpNote.

Panel reach is narrow: 'synth.osc-wave' maps only to Pure/Sync/Super (bridge.ts:123-128), so the required Multi and FM-H categories cannot be selected from the surface at all; 'synth.filter-type' has no binding; every synth knob writes to layer 0 only, so S2/S3 are levels-only; there is no layer enable and no arp range/direction/hold control.

What does work: three layers with independent effect chains and independent state exist (synth.ts:105-135), poly/mono/legato voice allocation is correct (3 voices poly, 1 mono), unison spawns detuned voices (4 voices at unison 3), and all of it round-trips through the program.

criteria.label: Distinct engine behavior
evidence: Synth source families render identically: raw pairwise cross-correlation 0.9995-1.0000 for all ten Pure/Sync/Multi/Super/FM-H pairs at 48 kHz, each a saturated rail with 1 zero crossing per 0.2 s — the categories are renamed paths into a filter that diverges before the waveform matters.

Organ models are partly distinct once permitted reuse and DC are accounted for: with the DC component removed, B3 vs Vox 0.9993 (a genuine violation — Vox is required-distinct), B3 vs Pipe1 0.827, Farf 0.69-0.85 against the rest. Pipe1 vs Pipe2 is exactly 1.000 because Pipe2 is Pipe1 scaled by 1.35 (organ.ts:60-68), and B3 vs Bass 0.949 — both are spec-permitted reuses ('may-reuse-Pipe-1', 'may-reuse-B3').

The candidate's own distinctness proofs cannot detect any of this: tests/organ.test.ts:93-99 and tests/synth.test.ts:60-67 assert |rms(a) - rms(b)| > 1e-4 / 1e-5 between scalar RMS values, which passes trivially on DC rails and on gain-scaled copies.

Real distinctions that do exist: drawbar registration changes the organ spectrum (centroid 148 Hz -> 767 Hz), Farf's square/register engine is genuinely separate, Pipe 1's ranks and 20 ms attack differ from B3's, and the Piano library types remain distinct from Phase 2.

criteria.label: Inherited graph and effects integration
evidence: One context, one destination, verified live: instrumenting window.AudioContext before loading dist recorded exactly 1 AudioContext and 1 ScriptProcessorNode across a full session; artifact/src/audio/graph4.ts:49-60 wires drain -> masterGain (Master Level) -> DynamicsCompressor limiter -> context.destination, and dispose() clears the handler, disconnects all three nodes and closes the context (graph4.ts:71-79).

All engines are mixed inside System4 before the master path (artifact/src/audio/system4.ts:556-574: piano + organ + synth summed, master gain applied, then limiting), so nothing bypasses the master — confirmed by tests/system.test.ts:236-248 and by independent rendering at 48 kHz.

Per-layer chains keep the documented order Mod1 -> Mod2 -> Delay -> AmpSim/EQ -> Compressor -> Reverb (artifact/src/audio/chain.ts:29,103-110), with the organ's two layers sharing one chain, three independent synth chains, and one shared Rotary applied after reverb for routed layers (organ.ts:239, synth per-layer chains).

Integration gaps: the effects section's routing controls (fx.focus-piano/organ/synth-s1..s3, fx.group, fx.delay/comp/reverb-global, fx.to-rotary-a/b, fx.rotary-on, fx.rotary-speed) are handled only by the superseded artifact/src/piano/bridge.ts:80-120, which App.tsx no longer calls, so effect targeting/global modes are unreachable in Phase 3; the effect knobs that are bound all write to piano.chains[0] (bridge.ts:150-177). Because the criterion's guidance names targeting, a rating of 2 is defensible; 3 is kept because the topology, gain staging and cleanup that dominate it are correct.

The drain is a deprecated ScriptProcessorNode with a 256-frame buffer on the main thread (graph4.ts:49) — the only console output during the interaction pass is Chromium's ScriptProcessorNode deprecation warning.

criteria.label: Musical quality, latency, and load
evidence: The shipped app is silent in a normal browser. The AudioContext is created during the first render (App.tsx:57-61) and resume() appears nowhere in src or in dist/assets/index-u1Bg_2yK.js (grep count 0). Serving artifact/dist under the default Chromium autoplay policy: context.state = 'suspended' before interaction and still 'suspended' after clicking the surface and holding a key, with 0 audioprocess callbacks and no output. The identical build with --autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required reaches 'running' with 313 callbacks, isolating the cause to the missing resume-on-gesture.

Non-finite samples take over the master output on real programs: capturing the output buffer per factory program, '4.4 FM Bell' rendered 19132/20480 non-finite samples on a low key and 20480/20480 on a high key, and '5.5 Band Layered' rendered 20480/20480 on both — the corruption is at the master path, so the piano and organ layers in those programs are destroyed too.

With the context forced to run, the synth is a DC rail rather than a note ('4.1 Synth Pad' measured dc -0.372 with 6 zero crossings in 20480 samples) and the organ carries a DC offset roughly 3x its AC content ('3.2 B3 Organ': dc 0.186, ac-rms 0.055).
Sustained full-scale clipping: an FM-H layer with delay + reverb enabled settles at rms 0.990 / peak 0.990 / dc 0.990 from block 1 onward at 48 kHz — the limiter rail, not a decaying note.

What holds up: the Piano remains musical through the master path ('1.1 Grand Piano' measured peak 0.071/0.095, 831 and 3219 zero crossings, no DC and no NaN), Panic silences everything instantly (post-Panic rms 0.000000), and voice accounting returns to baseline — 60 voices across three engines after 20 notes, 0 after release plus ~8 s of rendering; layered/split programs render without dropouts and no console errors appear during the pass.

criteria.label: Canonical state round-trip
evidence: ProgramState is a genuine canonical contract covering piano (2 layers + chains), organ (2 layers, shared chain, drawbars, percussion, key click, vibrato/chorus, rotary speed/drive), synth (3 layers + 3 chains), split/zones/crossfades, scenes, morph assignments, clock and transpose (artifact/src/system/program.ts:189-199).

Store then reload restores it exactly at the canonical level: tests/system.test.ts:41-68 compares the full JSON of slot 12 after a rich edit, and program loads demonstrably reach the engines — the same key renders piano on '1.1 Grand Piano' (zc 831, no DC), a DC-heavy organ on '3.2 B3 Organ' (dc 0.135) and a rail on '4.1 Synth Pad' (dc -0.372).

Dirty/discard is truthful at the engine level: edits set dirty, Store clears it, selecting another program discards without touching the stored slot (system4.ts:177-192, verified in dist as 'P1.1' -> 'P1.1E' -> Store x2 -> 'P1.1').
Master Level is correctly excluded from program state per the spec (system4.ts:418-424, asserted in tests/system.test.ts:80-90).

But the criterion's guidance also requires focus and display state to be restored, and neither is: nothing writes program values back into the hardware store (App.tsx:160-165 syncs only the two OLED strings), so after any program change all 236 controls still show the previous patch — measured across six factory programs, including a split program whose Split button reads false and an organ program whose drawbars do not move. Combined with the delta-only bridge, this makes controls silently no-op when their stale value already matches the program. Morph assignments round-trip as data but cannot be created or heard from the surface.

criteria.label: Required hardware bindings
evidence: Audit of artifact/src/hardware/sections.ts vs artifact/src/system/bridge.ts: 139 declared ids (134 controls plus 5 section ids); 37 are absent from the Phase 3 bridge, of which 8 prog.btn-* are handled by the edge-triggered navigation loop and 4 are displays/branding. The remaining inert non-excluded controls are fx.focus-piano, fx.focus-organ, fx.focus-synth-s1/s2/s3, fx.group, fx.delay-global, fx.comp-global, fx.reverb-global, fx.rotary-on, fx.rotary-speed, fx.to-rotary-a, fx.to-rotary-b, synth.filter-type, piano.on, piano.layer-a-focus, piano.layer-b-focus, piano.model, perf.mod-wheel and perf.pitch-stick — all Phase 2/3 required behaviour, not spec exclusions (PSTICK is required by the piano spec; effects group/global modes by effects.routing).

Cross-checked against every spec's scope.excluded: only prog.morph-after (aftertouch as a morph source) is genuinely spec-excluded among the inert controls. The exclusion list itself lives in an exported constant that nothing references (artifact/src/system/program.ts:202-212, grep UNSUPPORTED -> declaration only) and is surfaced only as prose in IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json, never in the product.

Bound-but-wrong: the nine drawbars write a 0..1 normalised value into a 0..8 field (controls.tsx:127-133 vs bridge.ts:77-85), measured as aria-valuenow 8 -> 1 -> 0 after two ArrowDown presses; every effects knob writes to piano.chains[0] only; every synth knob writes to synth.layers[0] only; organ model buttons overwrite both organ layers.

Missing bindings for required behaviour: no control enables/disables the organ or synth sections or their layers, no control selects split point / crossfade / zone, no control drives morph interpolation, and no control selects the Multi or FM-H synth categories.

The Phase 2 bindings for these same ids still exist in artifact/src/piano/bridge.ts:80-120 but that module is imported only by tests/piano-effects.test.ts:6 — the passing test no longer reflects the shipped app.

criteria.label: Cross-system workflows
evidence: The architecture for cross-system behaviour is real: one System4 owns programs, scenes, zones, clock, transpose and Panic and routes every note through transpose -> scene mask -> zone/crossfade gain -> engine (artifact/src/audio/system4.ts:512-542), program changes propagate coherently to the engines and the OLED, and the clock is shared by LFO and arp step computation (synth.ts:244-247,400-406).

But the integrated workflows cannot actually be exercised. The '5.1 Split' program cannot demonstrate split routing at all: its organ zone covers MIDI < 60 while the only working input (the computer keyboard) spans 60..83, so both a 'low' and a 'high' key land in the piano zones — measured output on that program is piano on both keys (dc 0.000, zc 1545 and 3177, rms 0.021 each), with the organ (rms ~0.145, heavy DC) never sounding.
The flagship all-engine program '5.5 Band Layered' renders 20480/20480 non-finite samples at the master output on every key tried, so the layered workflow produces no usable audio at all.

Effect focus/targeting is inert, the morph layer cannot be exercised from the surface, the arpeggiator never reaches audio, and the panel does not follow the loaded program, so no multi-system edit can be seen or continued from the hardware.

Keyboard-driven play is the only working note path in the shipped build (pointer and touch fail, see regressionReliability), and only after the autoplay policy is overridden — which limits the layered/split workflow to something a user cannot reach at all.

criteria.label: Inherited regression reliability
evidence: Phase 1 pointer/touch input is broken in the built app: .keys-white and .keys-black are both position:absolute; inset:0 (artifact/src/styles.css:543) and the black-key container is painted last, so it hit-tests over the whole keybed. document.elementFromPoint at 5%, 25%, 50%, 75% and 95% of the keybed width returns the .keys-black container at every point, and clicking the keybed pressed 0 of 73 keys (aria-pressed false everywhere) with zero audio; touch emulation also fails. Dispatching pointerdown directly on a key element does work, which is why the jsdom tests in tests/interaction.test.tsx still pass.
Keybed geometry regression (see referenceRetention): 73 elements, 1 inside the viewport, 0 black keys visible — present in stage1/2/3 evidence captures alike.
Phase 2 effects routing regression: focus, group, global, To Rotary and Rotary controls no longer affect the engine in Phase 3 because App.tsx uses only src/system/bridge.ts (see hardwareBindings).

What survives: computer-keyboard note input works and is musical, the piano library reports ready and renders audibly, Master Level, the effect DSP units, sustain, status strip, Panic and the six-section responsive surface are all still functional (390x844: scrollWidth == clientWidth == 390, 6 sections, 236 controls); all 151 inherited and new tests pass.

Sample provenance regression risk: the bundled WAVs under public/samples are never fetched by the app (0 requests to /samples during a full session) and are not valid RIFF files — scripts/generate-samples.mjs writes the magic big-endian, so every file starts 'FFIR' (bytes 46 46 49 52 in public/samples/grand/58-v95.wav). The loader defaults to a no-op that always reports ready (artifact/src/piano/library.ts:41,57-61), so the status strip claims 'Piano library ready (sample sets + synthesis)' without loading anything.

criteria.label: System architecture
evidence: Clear ownership: canonical serializable state in src/system/program.ts, defaults/factory programs in src/system/factory.ts, morph path application in src/system/morph.ts, engine composition in src/audio/system4.ts, per-layer chains in src/audio/chain.ts, and the browser boundary isolated in src/audio/graph4.ts with an injectable contextFactory.

Engine boundaries are respected: StageEngine (piano), OrganEngine and SynthEngine each render mono blocks through their own chains into one mix, with a single shared Rotary instance passed in by the orchestrator (system4.ts:121-126).
Serialization/extensibility is good — serialize()/hydrate() cover both banks (system4.ts:295-311) and adding an engine means adding a LayerRef plus a REF_TO_ENUM entry.

Weaknesses: the hardware binding is one-way by construction (store -> program only), with no path from program state back to the surface, which is the root cause of the panel desync; the Phase 3 bridge keeps module-global mutable state (lastState, heldSource, holdSnap in src/system/bridge.ts:66-70), so two instruments or two tests in one process share edge-detection state; src/piano/bridge.ts and src/audio/graph.ts/engine.ts remain as a parallel, now-dead Phase 2 path still referenced by tests; and the sample 'library' is a no-op loader over an in-process generator, so the asset boundary the plan describes does not exist at runtime.

criteria.label: Tests and maintainability
evidence: Breadth is real: 16 test files / 151 tests, all passing on an independent install (and tsc --noEmit clean), with tests/feature-matrix.json mapping all 38 required feature ids to non-empty files.

But the audio-distinctness tests cannot fail for the defects present: tests/organ.test.ts:93-99 and tests/synth.test.ts:60-67 compare scalar RMS with tolerances of 1e-4/1e-5, which pass on DC rails and on Pipe2 = 1.35 x Pipe1; tests/splits.test.ts:56-66 'the 11 documented split positions are modeled' asserts the length and spacing of two literal arrays declared inside the test; the adjacent 'up to 4 zones' test assigns a value and asserts it back; tests/organ.test.ts:132-138 asserts the drawbar LED value is between 0 and 8; tests/synth.test.ts:177-240 checks eng.arpNote rather than rendered audio.
No test renders a factory program end-to-end, which is why two of the nine factory programs producing 100% non-finite output at the master path ships with a green suite.

Coverage holes align with the product gaps: no test drives the Phase 3 bridge for effect focus/global/rotary ids, no test covers Store As or the numeric list view through the UI, no test asserts the unsupported-control list, and hardware.bindings maps to tests that never enumerate control ids against bindings.

The jsdom-only DOM tests cannot see layout or hit-testing, which is why a keybed that renders as one 1301px slab and swallows all pointer input still passes tests/interaction.test.tsx and tests/regression.test.tsx.

Positives: naming and file layout are consistent, doc comments are substantial and mostly accurate about intent, and the graph tests do assert one context / one destination / disconnect counts across an injected boundary (tests/system.test.ts:212-234).

criteria.label: Runtime performance
evidence: Console is clean: loading dist and running a full interaction pass (programs, store, live, split, scenes, drawbars, wheel, transpose, panic, sustained keys) produced no errors or page errors at 1440x900 or 390x844 — only Chromium's ScriptProcessorNode deprecation warning, matching evidence/stage3-capture.json.

Cleanup is correct: voiceCount returned to 0 after 20 notes released plus ~8 s of rendering; post-Panic master output rms is 0.000000; SystemGraph.dispose() disconnects drain/master/limiter and closes the context; App unmount detaches keyboard, MIDI and lifecycle (App.tsx:82-93).
Rendering the whole instrument in a main-thread ScriptProcessorNode with a 256-frame buffer (graph4.ts:49) is a latency/underrun risk by construction; an AudioWorklet is the supported path.

Numerical stability problems surface at runtime: whole-buffer non-finite output on the FM and layered factory programs, and a sustained full-scale DC rail (0.99) once delay/reverb are engaged on a synth layer.

React re-render behaviour is acceptable (store-driven useSyncExternalStore, memoised sections) but the bridge rebuilds the whole working program via JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...)) on every hardware change (bridge.ts:221).

issues.title: AudioContext is never resumed, so the shipped app is silent in a normal browser
issues.detail: App.tsx:57-61 constructs SystemGraph (and its AudioContext) during the first render, before any user gesture, and resume() does not appear in src or in dist/assets/index-u1Bg_2yK.js. Serving artifact/dist with default Chromium autoplay policy, context.state stayed 'suspended' before and after clicking the surface and holding keys, with 0 audioprocess callbacks and no output; the same build launched with --autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required reaches 'running' with hundreds of callbacks. All audio in this evaluation had to be measured with that override.

issues.title: Keybed renders as a single blank slab and pointer/touch note input does not work
issues.detail: src/hardware/keys.ts emits unit coordinates (x = white-key index, width = 1) that src/components/Keybed.tsx:68 writes as CSS percentages, so key E1 is 1301px wide at left 70px and F1 sits at left 1370px (style left 100%); 1 of 73 keys falls inside a 1440x900 viewport and no black keys are visible. In addition .keys-black is position:absolute; inset:0 above the white layer (styles.css:543), so document.elementFromPoint returns the black-key container at every point across the keybed and clicks and taps press nothing (verified: 0 of 73 keys pressed, zero audio; synthetic pointerdown on the element does work, which is why jsdom tests pass). The same slab appears in the artifact's own stage1/2/3 evidence captures.

issues.title: Synth engine outputs a saturated DC rail instead of a waveform; all source categories identical
issues.detail: A Pure/Sine voice at A440 with the chain bypassed, res 0, keytrack 0, no filter envelope renders dc 0.6984 / ac-rms 0.0326 with 1 zero crossing in 0.2 s at 48 kHz and at every cutoff tried. The SVF in src/audio/synth.ts:349-357 is unconditionally unstable: its state matrix [[1+u,-u],[-u,1]] with u = g/(1+g(g+k)) has eigenvalue 1 + u(1+sqrt5)/2 > 1 for all positive cutoffs, so the state diverges exponentially and the layer clamps at +/-1. Consequently Pure/Sync/Multi/Super/FM-H correlate 0.9995-1.0000 pairwise, and filter types HP and LP24 emit non-finite samples (7457 of 9600).

issues.title: Two factory programs render 100% non-finite samples at the master output
issues.detail: Capturing the master output buffer per factory program in dist: '4.4 FM Bell' produced 19132 of 20480 non-finite samples on one key and 20480 of 20480 on another; '5.5 Band Layered' — the flagship program combining piano, organ and synth — produced 20480 of 20480 on every key tried. Because the corruption is at the shared master path, the piano and organ layers in those programs are destroyed too. No test renders a factory program end-to-end, so this ships with a green suite.

issues.title: No panel control reflects the loaded program, and stale controls silently no-op
issues.detail: App.tsx:160-165 (reflectDisplays) writes only the two OLED strings; there is no program -> hardware-store path. Loading six factory programs in dist left every control at its previous value: 'Piano layer B on' false on a program that enables it, '8 foot drawbar' 8 and '16 foot drawbar' 0 on '3.2 B3 Organ' (program drawbars [6,4,8,6,4,2,1,0,0]), 'Split' false on '5.1 Split'. Because src/system/bridge.ts:218-233 applies deltas only, a control whose stale value already equals the program's does nothing at all — reproduced on '2.1 Upright Combo', where clicking 'Piano layer B on' produced no state change and no dirty 'E'.

issues.title: Vox is B3 minus two partials, and every non-Farf model rides a large DC offset
issues.detail: Of the four required-distinct engines (organ spec: B3, Vox, Farf, Pipe 1), Vox is not distinct: with the DC component removed, B3 vs Vox correlates 0.9993 at 48 kHz with identical drawbars, because organ.ts:47-56 defines Vox as the B3 partial list minus two partials and the spec's filtered/unfiltered mix drawbar is admittedly not implemented. B3 vs Pipe1 is 0.827 and Farf is 0.69-0.85 against everything, so those distinctions are genuine. Pipe2 = Pipe1 x 1.35 and Bass = B3 restricted to two drawbars are explicitly permitted reuses ('may-reuse-Pipe-1', 'may-reuse-B3') and are not defects. Separately, all non-Farf models carry a DC offset several times their AC content (0.55 + 0.45*sin blend, organ.ts:289): a single 8' drawbar renders dc 0.1227 against ac-rms 0.0668, and the B3 factory program measured dc 0.186 against ac-rms 0.055 in the browser.

issues.title: Arpeggiator/gate never reaches the audio path
issues.detail: src/audio/synth.ts:384-398 advances arpStep/arpNote, but arpNote is never read by renderLayer or osc(); rendering three held notes with arp.run false vs true yields a sum-absolute-difference of exactly 0. tests/synth.test.ts:177-240 asserts only the internal arpNote value, so the required synth.arp-gate behaviour is state-only.

issues.title: Morph interpolation cannot be exercised from the instrument and there is no Control Pedal
issues.detail: System4.setWheel/setPedal (src/audio/system4.ts:315-323) have no caller in src (only tests/splits.test.ts); moving the Modulation wheel in the built app changes aria-valuenow only. The surface has no control-pedal input (src/hardware/sections.ts:12-18) — only the prog.morph-pedal assign button — so the Wheel/Control Pedal morph assignment, interpolation, indicator and clearing behaviour exists only as engine API and tests.

issues.title: Split editing is a single hard-coded C4 toggle, and the low zone is unplayable
issues.detail: bridge.ts:207 maps the SPLIT button to System4.toggleSplit, which forces split.points.mid = 60 (system4.ts:264-270). No panel control selects any of the 11 documented split positions, sets Off/+-6/+-12 crossfade width, or assigns layers to zones, although the engine implements all three. Worse, no note below the split can be played at all: pointer input is dead and MIDI is unavailable, so the only working input is the computer keyboard, which spans MIDI 60..83 (src/piano/inputs.ts:12-14) — the '5.1 Split' program's organ zone (MIDI < 60) is unreachable, and both a 'low' and a 'high' key render piano only.

issues.title: About twenty non-excluded controls have no Phase 3 binding
issues.detail: fx.focus-piano/organ/synth-s1..s3, fx.group, fx.delay/comp/reverb-global, fx.rotary-on, fx.rotary-speed, fx.to-rotary-a/b, synth.filter-type, piano.on, piano.layer-a/b-focus, piano.model, perf.mod-wheel and perf.pitch-stick are absent from src/system/bridge.ts. Cross-checking every spec's scope.excluded confirms only prog.morph-after is genuinely excluded; PSTICK is required by the piano spec and effects group/global modes by effects.routing. The effects ids are still handled by the superseded src/piano/bridge.ts, which only tests import, so Phase 2 effect targeting/global/rotary routing regressed at the product level while its test stayed green. Multi and FM-H synth categories are also unreachable (bridge.ts:123-128), and no control enables organ or synth layers. The UNSUPPORTED list (src/system/program.ts:202-212) is referenced nowhere in src or tests.

issues.title: Drawbar controls write a normalised value into a 0..8 field
issues.detail: DrawbarControl passes value/8 to useDragValue and writes the resulting 0..1 number back to the store (src/components/controls/controls.tsx:127-133), while sections.ts and bridge.ts:77-85 treat the same id as 0..8. Measured in the built app: '8 foot drawbar' goes 8 -> 1 -> 0 on two ArrowDown presses, making organ registration unusable from the panel.

issues.title: Visual audit asserts behaviour the sealed build does not have
issues.detail: evidence/stage3-visual-audit.md claims 'continuous tiled white keys with black keys centered on the seams' (the same file's screenshot shows a blank slab), 'up to 4 zones editable across the 11 documented split positions ... Off/+-12 crossfades', 'Wheel and Control Pedal morphs assign, interpolate, light their morph indicators and clear' as exercised surface flows, 'two-stage STORE, STORE AS naming' (no Store As affordance exists anywhere in src), and 'Drawbar LED ladders track the live 0-8 positions' (the LED graph controls expose aria-valuenow null and no control tracks a loaded program). None of those are editable or observable from the panel in the shipped app.

issues.title: Bundled WAV sample sets are never loaded and are not valid RIFF files
issues.detail: A full session against dist issued 0 requests for /samples; src/piano/library.ts:41 defaults the loader to a no-op that always reports 'ready' while the tables are regenerated in-process, so the status strip claims 'Piano library ready (sample sets + synthesis)' without loading anything. scripts/generate-samples.mjs writes the RIFF magic big-endian, so every file begins 'FFIR' (bytes 46 46 49 52 in public/samples/grand/58-v95.wav). IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json is honest that the material is generated rather than recorded, but its claim that the libraries are 'rendered as committed WAV assets under public/samples' is not borne out at runtime.

issues.title: Transpose readout does not update when transpose changes
issues.detail: System4.setTranspose (src/audio/system4.ts:395-397) mutates working state without emit(), so the status-strip value only refreshes on an unrelated re-render; two 'Transpose up' clicks left the displayed value at 0 in the built app, and it jumped to '+2' only after a later unrelated edit.

issues.title: Whole instrument is rendered in a 256-frame ScriptProcessorNode on the main thread
issues.detail: src/audio/graph4.ts:49 uses createScriptProcessor(256, 0, 2); Chromium emits the deprecation warning on every load and this path is prone to underruns under React re-render load. An AudioWorklet is the supported equivalent.

issues.title: Edge detection and morph-hold state are module globals
issues.detail: src/system/bridge.ts:66-70 keeps lastState, heldSource and holdSnap at module scope, so two System4 instances (or two tests in one process) share program-navigation edge detection and morph capture state; the bridge also deep-clones the entire program via JSON on every hardware change (bridge.ts:221).
